successors.name: Hittite Empire
successors.text: Kizzuwatna, which 'rebelled during Suppiluliuma I's reign but stayed inside the Hittite Empire for roughly two centuries'

ledger.x: c. 1500 BC: Kizzuwatna appears in the Cilician plain. The page gives no founding year; it is 'attested in written sources from the end of the 16th century BC onwards'. The Hittites page has Telepinu (c. 1500 BC) 'allying himself with one Hurrian state (Kizzuwatna) against another'; the Telipinu page (reign c. 1525 -…

c. 1480 BC: Kizzuwatna is a Mitanni vassal. The Idrimi page has the tablet that 'dates back to c. 1480 BC. It was a treaty that Idrimi made with another vassal ruler to Mitanni, Pilliya of Kizzuwatna.' The start of the Mitanni overlordship is not dated on any page; 1480 is the first dated evidence of it.

c. 1400 BC: Tudhaliya I frees Kizzuwatna from Mitanni. 'He made a treaty with Sunassura and freed Kizzuwatna from Mitanni's control' (paraphrase of the page, which gives no year). The year is the Hittites page's date for Tudhaliya I ('Tudhaliya I (c. 1400 BC) again allied with Kizzuwatna, then vanquished the Hurrian…

c. 1350 BC (bridged): Kizzuwatna is absorbed by Hatti. The page says only that Kizzuwatna 'rebelled during Suppiluliuma I's reign but stayed inside the Hittite Empire for roughly two centuries' and gives no year; Suppiluliuma 'came to the throne around 1350 BC' on the Arzawa page.

c. 1350 BC (bridged): the kingdom of Kizzuwatna ends as a separate state in the Hittite Empire, which it supplied with troops at Kadesh (c. 1274 BC) and in which it stayed until the Sea Peoples' time (c. 1200 BC); Quwe (Hiyawa) later 'emerged in the former territory of Kizzuwatna'.

wars.name: Tudhaliya I's campaign against Aleppo and Mitanni
wars.outcome: Hittite victory: Tudhaliya I 'again allied with Kizzuwatna, then vanquished the Hurrian states of Aleppo and Mitanni'; Kizzuwatna leaves Mitannian domination by treaty with Sunassura.

wars.name: Kizzuwatna's rebellion under Suppiluliuma I
wars.outcome: Kizzuwatna 'rebelled during Suppiluliuma I's reign but stayed inside the Hittite Empire for roughly two centuries'; annexed.

certainty.note: The only boundaries on the page are natural: the Taurus, the Amanus and the sea.
